Reap
REEP
v.
Webster 1828 prints REAP as verb transitive (to cut grain with a sickle; to clear a field; to gather as the fruit of labor or of works, in a good or bad sense) and as verb intransitive (to perform the act of reaping; to receive the fruit of labor). Related to Latin rapio, carpo; English crop. Companion pages already treat harvest, sow, and seed.

Biblical Definition

Reap is one spelling with two honest senses. Do not mash them.

1. To cut grain; to gather a field. To reap is to cut grain with a sickle, and so to clear a crop. When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not wholly reap the corners. Reaping is work under a law of mercy: leave the gleanings.

2. To receive the fruit of what was sown. Whatsoever a man sows, that he will also reap. Those who sow in tears shall reap in joy. The harvest can be corruption or life. The dictionary therefore keeps reap from becoming karma merch or a hustle proverb. God is not mocked. A man does not get wheat from thorns by branding the field.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828: REAP, verb transitive — to cut grain with a sickle; to clear of a crop; to gather or obtain as the fruit of labor or of works, in a good or bad sense. REAP, verb intransitive — to perform the act of reaping; to receive the fruit of labor or works.

expand to see more

REAP, verb transitive [Latin rapio, carpo; Gr. a sickle, to reap; Eng. crop.]

1. To cut grain with a sickle; as, to reap wheat or rye.

When ye reap the harvest, thou shalt not wholly reap the corners of thy field. Leviticus 19:9.

2. To clear of a crop by reaping; as, to reap a field.

3. To gather; to obtain; to receive as a reward, or as the fruit of labor or of works; in a good or bad sense; as, to reap a benefit from exertions.

He that soweth to the flesh, shall of the flesh reap corruption. Galatians 6:7.

REAP, verb intransitive

1. To perform the act or operation of reaping.

2. To receive the fruit of labor or works.

They that sow in tears, shall reap in joy. Psalms 126:5.

Key Scripture

Galatians 6:7 — "Do not be deceived, God is not mocked; for whatever a man sows, that he will also reap."

Psalm 126:5 — "Those who sow in tears Shall reap in joy."

Modern Corruption

Reap is corrupted when sowing and reaping is recast as karma or manifestation, when harvest is treated as a grindset trophy, and when mercy at the corners of the field is skipped as inefficiency.

expand to see more

The first corruption is karma with a Bible font. Galatians 6:7 is God is not mocked — not the universe keeping score, not manifestation, not a vision board. A man reaps what he sows because God judges, not because the cosmos is a vending machine.

The second corruption is grindset harvest. Reaping becomes a personal-brand trophy. Psalm 126:5 is sow in tears, reap in joy — a restoration promise, not a productivity hack.

The third corruption is efficiency against gleaning. Leviticus still forbids wholly reaping the corners. A field stripped to the fence is not faithfulness. It is refusing the poor the share God assigned.
